source_excerpts.text:
I completed a **finite-speed controller proof candidate**, preserving the earlier Tanner construction.

It replaces the engineered repair jumps with a specified static Hamiltonian, **8n controller qubits, and 8n single-qubit loss channels**. The candidate retains exponentially long protection of all encoded qubits, both CSS sectors, and a persistent bath, while allowing noisy controllers with arbitrary initial states and correlations. [Proof](<producer-workspace/PROOF.txt>).

Exact branch-record and overlapping-CSS algebra checks passed, alongside finite-speed operator diagnostics. These support the derivation at their finite scope; independent audit remains pending. [Results](<producer-workspace/RESULT.txt>).

The consequential remaining gap is the **large syndrome-dependent Hamiltonian**. Its bounded-arity implementation, physical wiring, reservoir accuracy, and power costs remain unearned. Finite rates, controller faults, thermal excitation, and reset activity are explicitly accounted for in the [resource analysis](<producer-workspace/RESOURCES_AND_BASELINE.txt>).

Lossy-ancilla simulation is established [prior work](https://arxiv.org/html/1506.04311); novelty of this all-time extension remains undetermined. No practical advantage over the [scheduled Tanner baseline](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.03684v1) is established.

FINITE-RESPONSE TANNER REPAIR WITH ONE-QUBIT LOSS
1 November 2026. Solo analytic proof candidate; independent audit and
priority assessment are not claimed. The older Tanner proof is unchanged.

Claim at its actual scope
========================
Assume the code family and density/confinement lemma in
../tanner_global_phase_20261101/DENSITY_LEMMA.txt. There is a static,
bounded-graph-local Hamiltonian on n data and 8n controller qubits whose
ONLY nominal Lindblad jumps are 8n ordinary one-qubit lowering operators.
All rates and interaction neighborhoods are finite constants independent
of n and storage time. For sufficiently small, fixed local-generator
perturbation density, this model protects all k=Omega(n) logical qubits
for time exponential in n, in joint diamond norm with the controllers and
an arbitrary finite persistent bath. Controllers may start in ANY state,
including correlations with the logical input, bath, and reference.

This is a generator-model theorem candidate, not a laboratory realization
or a few-body Hamiltonian compiler. The large syndrome-dependent
Hamiltonian and expanding connectivity remain explicit resources.

A. Data inputs, selected instrument, and notation
================================================
Use the original notation c=Delta^2, n=c m/2, M=C_R n sector/centers,
C_R=8/c, and commuting integer potential U=U_X+U_Z. Every local U_a is
between 0 and c; every data qubit meets four such factors. The original
density lemma supplies constants s,rho>0 such that, on the safe syndrome
domain below, there are >=s U active sector/centers, and w<=c U.

At center v, Pi_vF selects the FIRST strictly improving nonempty subset F
in the original fixed ordering. J_vF=Q_F Pi_vF. Thus

 Pi_vF Pi_vH=0 (F!=H),  J_vF^dagger J_vF=Pi_vF,
 Pi_v0=I-sum_(F!=0)Pi_vF.                               (A1)

The Q_F are the original pure-X or pure-Z Pauli writes, of weight <=c.
The data support of the whole center table is <=R_0=c+2c^2.
No coherent sum of the J_vF is substituted for their instrument.

For r=floor(rho n), let P select data syndromes with minimum SUMMED CSS
filling weight w<r, including every logical coordinate and every

support bound specified in C. Multiplying a Q-qubit Pauli changes w by

source_excerpts.text:
FINITE-SPEED CONTROLLER EXTENSION: RESULT AT ITS ACTUAL SCOPE
1 November 2026, solo work in this folder.

The prior complete Tanner proof candidate and corrected selected-center
instrument are unchanged. A new analytic proof candidate replaces their
large engineered dissipative jumps by a specified static Hamiltonian and
8n ordinary one-qubit loss channels on 8n record qubits.

The direct joint data/controller moment is exp(beta U+lambda N), in a
finite-depth analytical unitary frame. The entire first-order coupling
effect cancels on data observables, on all controller states. Second-order
ground blocks give the intended separate ACTIVE repair outcomes and an
innocuous syndrome Hamiltonian. Residual excited-controller blocks are
absorbed by physical loss drift; higher orders leave a small constant
source. This is an all-time drift argument for finite Gamma,g, rather
than an O(nT) adiabatic-channel approximation.

For a sufficiently small fixed local-generator norm density, the candidate
establishes, for all logical/C/B/reference inputs,

 inf_(Lambda_CB CPTP)
 ||Dec Phi_T Enc - Id_all-k tensor Lambda_CB||_diamond
 <= min(2, 12n[A_phys T+256epsilon] exp(-bn/2)).

Here k=Omega(n), b>0, epsilon=g/Gamma>0, and A_phys are fixed constants,
independent of n and storage horizon. Both CSS sectors and a common,
arbitrary finite persistent bath are retained. Controllers may start in
arbitrary states and correlations. Controller faults, thermal gain, jump
miscalibration and continuous coherent couplings are charged in one norm
budget. No extra physical startup reset, frame-changing gates, global
schedule, healthy exterior, or completed-channel replacement is used.

PROOF.txt provides the construction, explicit sufficient parameter order,
the local Taylor/Schur estimates, initialization and output-frame argument,
and the CP/TNI boundary/diamond-norm conclusion. It inherits the previous
Tanner density lemma and code-family assumptions. It is a solo analytic
proof candidate; an independent audit is not claimed.

Finite controls:
 - 32 exact full-data-basis checks of a three-outcome branch register,
   including nonzero record detuning and the full Poisson inverse.
 - 16 exact basis checks for two overlapping, noncommuting CSS couplers,
   including 32 per-center second-order ground identities and frame order.
 - 12 finite-speed full-generator weighted-operator diagnostics.
